en: to be reinforced; to be strengthened

examples.en: The rules get stricter from this year.
Security has been tightened, so entry is hard.
Your muscles get stronger when you exercise.
The strengthened law starts next week.
Once enforcement tightened, accidents decreased.
For the relationship to grow stronger, you need to meet often.

explain: 규칙, 보안, 단속처럼 기준이 더 엄해질 때 자주 써요. 힘이나 관계가 더 단단해질 때도 쓰고요. 반대말은 '약화되다'예요. 뉴스에서 많이 들어요.

phrases.en: The school strengthens security.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이나 기관이 직접 더 엄하게 할 때 써요. 저절로 되면 '강화되다'예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a person or organization makes something stricter. When it just happens, use '강화되다'.

phrases.en: Enforcement will be tightened even more next year.
phrases.nuance_ko: '더'를 붙여 이미 엄한 것이 더욱 엄해진다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: '더' adds the sense of getting stricter than before.

phrases.en: The school rules became stricter.
phrases.nuance_ko: '강화되다'보다 쉽고 일상 대화에서 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier word than '강화되다', more common in everyday talk.

explain_en: It is common when standards such as rules, security or enforcement become stricter. It also fits strength or relationships becoming firmer. Its opposite is '약화되다', and you hear it a lot in the news.

examples.ko: 금융 당국이 은행의 재무 건전성을 점검했어요.
examples.en: Financial authorities checked the banks' financial soundness.
The government said it would improve fiscal soundness.
I don't invest in companies with low financial soundness.
We discussed the wholesomeness of content for teenagers.

examples.ko: 대출 건전성 평가가 이번 달에 발표돼요.
examples.en: The loan soundness assessment will be announced this month.
The sounder a company is, the stronger it is in a crisis.

explain: '건전하다'에 '-성'이 붙은 말로, 뉴스에서는 '재정 건전성', '재무 건전성'처럼 빚이 적고 운영이 안정적인지를 말할 때 많이 나와요. '건전성이 높다/낮다'로 말해요. 내용이나 문화가 바른지 말할 때도 써요.

phrases.example: 시청은 재정 건전성을 위해 지출을 줄였어요.
phrases.en: The city hall cut spending for the sake of fiscal soundness.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나라나 도시의 돈 관리가 안정적인지를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for how stable a country's or city's finances are.

phrases.example: 이 회사는 재무 건전성이 낮아서 위험해요.
phrases.en: This company has low financial soundness, so it's risky.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빚이 많거나 운영이 불안하다고 평가할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to judge that debt is high or operations are unstable.

phrases.en: The government is checking the soundness of the banks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 기관이나 금융 상태를 확인할 때 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common news phrase for inspecting the health of institutions or finances.

explain_en: It is '건전하다' plus '-성', and in the news it appears in '재정 건전성' and '재무 건전성', meaning low debt and stable operation. You say '건전성이 높다/낮다'. It can also be used for whether content or culture is wholesome.

en: to change rapidly; to undergo upheaval

examples.ko: 세상이 너무 빨리 격변해서 따라가기 힘들어요.
examples.en: The world is changing so fast that it is hard to keep up.
Korean society went through great upheaval in the 20th century.

examples.ko: 격변하는 시대에는 새로운 기술을 배워야 해요.
examples.en: In an era of rapid change, you have to learn new skills.

examples.ko: 시장이 격변하자 회사들이 계획을 다시 짰어요.
examples.en: When the market changed drastically, the companies redrew their plans.
As the climate changed drastically, farming became harder.

examples.ko: 격변했던 그 시절을 어머니는 지금도 자주 이야기하세요.
examples.en: My mother still often talks about those turbulent days.

explain: '변하다'보다 훨씬 급하고 크게 바뀐다는 뜻이라 사회, 시대, 시장 같은 큰 대상에 어울려요. 명사 '격변'이나 '격변기'(크게 바뀌는 시기)로도 많이 말해요.

phrases.example: 격변하는 세상에서 새로운 기술을 배워야 해요.
phrases.en: In a rapidly changing world, we have to learn new skills.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크게 빠르게 바뀌는 사회를 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Modifies a society that is changing fast and greatly.

phrases.example: 격변의 시대를 살아온 할머니 이야기를 들었어요.
phrases.en: I heard the story of my grandmother, who lived through an era of upheaval.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '격변'을 써서 시대를 말할 때 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun '격변' fits well when describing an era.

phrases.en: The late Joseon period was a time of upheaval when the country shook.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크게 바뀌는 시기를 한 단어로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: One word for a period of drastic change.

explain_en: It describes a much faster and bigger change than '변하다', so it suits large things like a society, an era or a market. The nouns '격변' and '격변기' (a time of great change) are also common.

en: reduction; easing (of a burden, pain, or penalty)

examples.ko: 세금 경감 소식에 가게 주인들이 기뻐했어요.
examples.en: Shop owners were glad to hear about the tax reduction.

examples.ko: 부담 경감을 위해 회의 횟수를 줄였어요.
examples.en: To ease the load, we cut down the number of meetings.
It's an exercise that helps relieve pain.

examples.ko: 이 약은 증상의 빠른 경감으로 유명해요.
examples.en: This medicine is known for quickly easing symptoms.
I asked whether the fine could be reduced.

examples.ko: 수업 시간 경감 덕분에 학생들이 여유를 찾았어요.
examples.en: Thanks to fewer class hours, the students found some breathing room.

explain: '부담 경감', '세금 경감'처럼 무거운 것을 덜어 줄 때 써요. 뉴스와 서류에서 자주 보는 딱딱한 말이에요. 경찰 계급에도 '경감'이 있어서 소리가 같지만 문맥으로 구별해요.

phrases.example: 정부가 가족의 부담 경감을 위한 대책을 발표했어요.
phrases.en: The government announced measures to ease the burden on families.
phrases.nuance_ko: '경감' 앞에 가장 자주 붙는 말로, 무거운 부담을 덜어 준다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common word before 경감; it means easing a heavy burden.

phrases.example: 세금 경감 덕분에 생활이 조금 편해졌어요.
phrases.en: Thanks to the tax reduction, life has become a little easier.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세금을 줄여 준다는 뜻으로 뉴스와 서류에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means reducing taxes; common in news and documents.

phrases.example: 이 운동은 통증 경감에 도움이 돼요.
phrases.en: This exercise helps relieve pain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아픔이 줄어드는 것을 딱딱하게 말할 때 써요. 일상에서는 '통증이 줄다'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal way to say pain gets less; in daily speech people say 통증이 줄다.

explain_en: Used in phrases like '부담 경감' and '세금 경감' when something heavy is lightened. It is a stiff word common in the news and in documents. There is also a police rank called '경감' that sounds the same, so tell them apart from context.

examples.en: National character differs a little from country to country.

examples.ko: 한국 사람의 국민성을 한마디로 말하기는 어려워요.
examples.en: It's hard to describe Korean national character in one word.

examples.ko: 이 소설은 영국의 국민성을 잘 보여 줘요.
examples.en: This novel shows British national character well.

examples.ko: 국민성은 역사와 환경의 영향을 받는다고 해요.
examples.en: They say national character is influenced by history and environment.
While traveling, I felt the national character of that country.

examples.ko: 국민성을 단정해서 말하는 것은 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: You should be careful about making definite claims about national character.

explain: 한 나라 사람들에게 두루 나타난다고 여겨지는 성격이나 태도를 말해요. '한국 사람은 빨리빨리 한다'처럼 흔히 하는 이야기가 여기에 들어가요. '민족성'과 비슷하지만 '국민성'은 민족이 아니라 나라를 기준으로 말해요.

phrases.en: The differences in national character between Korea and Japan are interesting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나라끼리 비교할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pair of words when comparing countries.

phrases.example: 이 경기는 우리 국민성을 잘 보여 줘요.
phrases.en: This match shows our national character well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일이 그 나라 사람들의 성격을 알려 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when an event shows what a country's people are like.

phrases.example: 어려울 때 그 나라의 국민성이 드러나요.
phrases.en: A country's national character shows in hard times.
phrases.nuance_ko: '보여 주다'는 하는 쪽이 있고, '드러나다'는 저절로 나타나는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: 보여 주다 has a doer; 드러나다 feels like it comes out naturally.

explain_en: It refers to traits or attitudes thought to be common among a country's people, like 'Koreans do things quickly'. It is similar to '민족성', but '국민성' is based on the nation rather than the ethnic group.

examples.en: The government said it would strengthen national defense.

examples.ko: 한 나라의 국방력은 군인 수만으로 정해지지 않아요.
examples.en: A country's defense capability isn't determined by the number of soldiers alone.

examples.ko: 국방력이 약하면 외교에서도 불리할 수 있다는 말이 있어요.
examples.en: Some say that weak defense can be a disadvantage in diplomacy too.

examples.ko: 국방력과 경제력을 함께 키워야 한다고 해요.
examples.en: They say we must build up both defense power and economic power.

examples.ko: 이 보고서는 세계 국방력 순위를 발표했어요.
examples.en: This report published a world ranking of defense power.
As technology advanced, the meaning of defense power changed too.

explain: '군사력'은 군대가 가진 힘을, 국방력은 나라를 지키는 전체 능력을 말할 때 더 자연스러워요. '강화하다', '키우다' 같은 말과 잘 어울리고 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: Each country works to build up its defense power.
phrases.nuance_ko: '강화하다'보다 조금 더 쉽고 부드럽게 들리는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A slightly easier and softer pairing than 강화하다.

phrases.example: 국방력이 강한 나라는 쉽게 공격받지 않아요.
phrases.en: A country with strong defense power is not easily attacked.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나라의 방어 능력을 평가할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when evaluating a country's ability to defend itself.

phrases.en: Strengthening national defense needs a large budget.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스 제목이나 정책 이야기에서 명사처럼 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used as a noun phrase in news headlines and policy talk.

explain_en: '군사력' fits better for the strength of the military itself, while 국방력 is more natural for a nation's overall ability to defend itself. It goes well with '강화하다' and '키우다' and often appears in the news.

examples.en: Agricultural mechanization greatly reduced the need for labor.
The factory's mechanization is almost complete.
As mechanization advanced, jobs changed.
Some people are worried because of mechanization.
The mechanization of rice planting happened long ago.
Thanks to mechanization, production speed increased.

explain: 사람이 하던 일을 기계가 대신하게 되는 변화예요. 농업, 공장, 산업 이야기에서 자주 나오고, '자동화'는 사람 손 없이 저절로 돌아가는 데 더 초점이 있어요.

phrases.en: These days most farm work has been mechanized.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 기계로 바뀌는 변화를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when work changes over to machines.

phrases.en: The company decided to mechanize the factory.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누가 일부러 기계로 바꿀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone deliberately switches to machines.

phrases.en: The mechanization of farming has sped up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 산업 이야기에서 자주 보는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase in talk about industry.

explain_en: It is the change of machines taking over work people used to do. It appears often in talk of farming, factories and industry, while '자동화' focuses more on things running by themselves without human hands.

examples.en: Our country is aging rapidly.
They say we must prepare for an aging society.
Rural areas lack workers because of an aging population.
We need policies to slow down population aging.
The problem of aging concerns all of us.
Even cities are not free from aging.

explain: 인구에서 나이 든 사람의 비율이 늘어나는 것을 말할 때 써요. '고령화'도 같은 뜻으로 쓰고, 한 사람의 몸이 늙는 것은 '노화'라고 해서 구별해요.

phrases.en: Our country has entered an aging society.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나이 든 사람의 비율이 높아진 사회를 말하는 대표적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The standard phrase for a society with a growing share of older people.

phrases.en: The speed of aging is faster than in other countries.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인구가 늙어 가는 빠르기를 비교할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to compare how fast a population is aging.

phrases.en: We have to solve the problem of an aging population.
phrases.nuance_ko: '노령화'와 같은 뜻이며, 뉴스에서는 '고령화'를 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 노령화; 고령화 is more common in the news.

explain_en: It is used when the share of older people in a population grows. '고령화' is used with the same meaning, while one person's body getting older is called '노화', which is a different word.

examples.ko: 저는 아직 무주택이라서 청약을 알아보고 있어요.
examples.en: I don't own a home yet, so I'm looking into the housing subscription.
They say households without a home get the chance first.
The longer you've gone without owning a home, the higher your score.
Many newlyweds don't own a home.

examples.ko: 무주택자를 위한 대출 상품이 새로 나왔어요.
examples.en: A new loan product for people without a home has come out.
Many people have gone a long time without owning a home.

explain: 자기 집이 없다는 뜻이라서 '무주택자', '무주택 가구'로 뉴스나 청약 안내에서 많이 나와요. 길에서 사는 '노숙'과는 달라서, 월세나 전세로 살아도 무주택이에요. 반대말은 '유주택'이에요.

phrases.en: Those without a home get more points in the housing lottery.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집이 없는 사람을 가리켜요. 청약 안내에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a person who owns no home. Common in housing application notices.

phrases.en: Support for households without a home has increased.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집이 없는 가족 단위를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a family unit that owns no home.

phrases.en: The longer your period without a home, the better.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집 없이 지낸 기간을 말하고, 청약 조건에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the time spent without owning a home, common in housing application conditions.
phrases.en_equiv: period of not owning a home

explain_en: It means not owning a home, and appears in news and housing-subscription notices as '무주택자' or '무주택 가구'. It is different from sleeping on the street: someone renting on 월세 or 전세 is still 무주택. The opposite is '유주택'.

examples.en: Marriage and inheritance are covered by civil law.

examples.ko: 민법에 따르면 계약은 두 사람의 합의로 이루어져요.
examples.en: According to the Civil Code, a contract is formed by agreement between two people.

examples.ko: 이웃과의 문제는 민법으로 해결할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can settle problems with neighbors under civil law.

examples.ko: 민법 수업이 너무 어려워서 공부를 많이 해야 해요.
examples.en: The civil law class is so hard that I have to study a lot.

examples.ko: 형법과 달리 민법은 개인 사이의 일을 다뤄요.
examples.en: Unlike criminal law, civil law deals with matters between individuals.
Civil law has to be applied to this case.

explain: '민법'은 사람들 사이의 재산, 계약, 가족 문제를 다루고, 범죄와 벌은 '형법'이 다뤄요. '민사 재판', '민사 사건'처럼 '민사'라는 말도 같이 알아 두면 좋아요.

phrases.en: They divide the property according to the Civil Code.
phrases.nuance_ko: 법에 근거해서 말할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say something is based on the law.

phrases.en: This case goes through a civil trial.
phrases.nuance_ko: '민법'과 관련된 재판을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A trial that deals with matters under civil law.

phrases.en: Theft is punished under the Criminal Code.
phrases.nuance_ko: '민법'과 반대로 범죄와 벌을 다루는 법이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Unlike '민법', this law deals with crimes and punishment.

explain_en: '민법' covers property, contracts and family matters between people, while crimes and punishment fall under '형법' (criminal law). It is also useful to know '민사', as in '민사 재판' (civil trial).

examples.en: This neighborhood has a low crime rate, so it's safe.
The crime rate is dropping a little every year.
The crime rate differs a lot from city to city.
I heard the crime rate fell after more streetlights were added.
The news said the youth crime rate has gone up.
What should we do to lower the crime rate?

explain: '높다/낮다', '늘다/줄다', '오르다/떨어지다'와 함께 써요. '실업률', '출산율'처럼 통계를 말할 때 붙는 '-률/-율'이에요. 뉴스와 토론 글에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 밤에 범죄율이 높은 지역은 조심해야 해요.
phrases.en: You should be careful in areas with a high crime rate at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안전하지 않은 지역을 설명할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to describe unsafe areas.

phrases.en: The police try to lower the crime rate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정책이나 뉴스에서 목표를 말할 때 많이 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common in policy talk and news when stating a goal.

phrases.en: When the economy gets worse, the crime rate sometimes goes up.
phrases.nuance_ko: '높다'는 상태를, '오르다'는 올라가는 변화를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: 높다 describes a state; 오르다 describes the change of rising.

explain_en: It goes with '높다/낮다' (high/low), '늘다/줄다' (increase/decrease) and '오르다/떨어지다' (rise/fall). The ending '-률/-율' is the same one in '실업률' and '출산율', used for statistics. It appears often in news and debate writing.

examples.ko: 부자와 가난한 사람의 격차가 점점 양극화하고 있어요.
examples.en: The gap between the rich and the poor is becoming more polarized.

examples.ko: 의견이 양극화해서 토론이 잘 안 돼요.
examples.en: Opinions are polarized, so the discussion isn't going well.

examples.ko: 사회가 양극화하면 갈등이 커질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If society polarizes, conflict can grow.

examples.ko: 소비도 비싼 것과 싼 것으로 양극화하는 추세예요.
examples.en: Spending is also trending toward polarization between expensive and cheap things.

examples.ko: 일자리가 좋은 곳과 나쁜 곳으로 양극화했다는 보고서가 나왔어요.
examples.en: A report came out saying jobs have polarized into good ones and bad ones.

examples.ko: 사람들의 생각이 양극화하지 않도록 서로 대화해야 해요.
examples.en: We need to talk with each other so that people's thinking doesn't polarize.

explain: 소득, 의견, 정치처럼 서로 반대되는 두 쪽으로 갈라지는 상황에 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '양극화가 심해지다', '양극화가 뚜렷하다'처럼 명사 형태로 더 많이 말하고, 동사형은 뉴스나 글에 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: Income polarization is getting worse these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사 대신 명사 '양극화'를 써서 일상 대화에서 더 자주 말하는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun 양극화 instead of the verb; this is the more common form in everyday speech.

phrases.en: When society becomes polarized, conflict grows.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로 갈라지기보다 어떤 상황 때문에 갈라진다는 느낌이 있어서 '양극화하다'와 함께 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Has a passive feel, as if split by circumstances; often used alongside 양극화하다.

phrases.en: In a polarized society, it is hard to understand each other.
phrases.nuance_ko: '양극화한'이 뒤의 명사를 꾸미는 형태로, 글이나 뉴스에서 많이 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form that describes a noun, common in writing and news.

explain_en: It is used when something splits into two opposing sides, such as income, opinions or politics. In everyday talk people more often use the noun form, as in '양극화가 심해지다' and '양극화가 뚜렷하다', while the verb form appears more in news and writing.

en: to be relaxed; to be eased

examples.en: The regulations will be eased from next month.

examples.ko: 약을 먹은 뒤에 통증이 조금 완화됐어요.
examples.en: After taking the medicine, the pain eased a little.
When the tension eased, I started to laugh.

examples.ko: 비자 조건이 완화되면 더 많은 사람이 올 거예요.
examples.en: If visa conditions are relaxed, more people will come.

examples.ko: 완화된 기준 덕분에 저도 신청할 수 있게 됐어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the relaxed standard, I became able to apply too.
As the weather warms up, the cold is easing.

explain: '완화되다'는 심하던 것이 약해질 때 써요. 규칙, 통증, 긴장, 갈등처럼 센 것이 부드러워지는 경우에 어울려요. 사람이 일부러 줄일 때는 '완화하다'이고, 저절로 그렇게 될 때가 '완화되다'예요.

phrases.en: The government eased the regulations.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이나 기관이 일부러 줄일 때 쓰는 능동 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The active form, used when someone deliberately eases something.

phrases.en: The tension eased after we talked.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음이나 분위기가 풀릴 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pair used when feelings or mood become less tense.

phrases.en: This medicine is good for pain relief.
phrases.nuance_ko: 약이나 치료 이야기에서 명사처럼 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used like a noun when talking about medicine or treatment.

explain_en: 완화되다 is used when something severe becomes milder, such as rules, pain, tension or conflict. When a person does it on purpose it is 완화하다, and when it happens by itself it is 완화되다.

examples.ko: 정부는 해외에 있는 자국민을 안전하게 데려오려고 노력했어요.
examples.en: The government worked to bring its citizens abroad home safely.

examples.ko: 자국민 보호는 모든 나라 정부의 중요한 일이에요.
examples.en: Protecting its own citizens is an important duty of every government.

examples.ko: 그 나라는 자국민과 외국인에게 다른 비자 규칙을 적용해요.
examples.en: That country applies different visa rules to its own citizens and to foreigners.

examples.ko: 대사관은 자국민에게 위험 지역에 가지 말라고 알렸어요.
examples.en: The embassy told its citizens not to go to dangerous areas.

examples.ko: 그 나라에는 자국민만 이용할 수 있는 복지 제도가 있어요.
examples.en: That country has a welfare program that only its own citizens can use.

examples.ko: 외국에서 사고를 당한 자국민이 있으면 영사관이 도와줘요.
examples.en: If one of its citizens has an accident abroad, the consulate helps them.

explain: '외국인'과 맞서는 말로, 뉴스나 정치 이야기에서 한 나라가 자기 나라 사람을 가리킬 때 써요. 일상에서 한국 사람 입장이면 '우리 국민'이라고도 말해요. 어느 나라 사람이든 '자기 나라' 기준으로 쓰기 때문에 '한국인'과 달리 나라가 정해져 있지 않아요.

phrases.example: 정부의 가장 큰 일은 자국민 보호예요.
phrases.en: The government's biggest job is protecting its own citizens.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 가장 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase in the news.

phrases.example: 이 서비스는 자국민과 외국인 모두 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Both citizens and foreigners can use this service.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말 '외국인'과 같이 나눠서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used together with its opposite, '외국인'.

phrases.example: 일부 나라는 일자리에서 자국민 우선 정책을 펴요.
phrases.en: Some countries have a citizens-first policy for jobs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 나라 사람을 먼저 챙기는 정책을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for policies that put one's own people first.

explain_en: It is the counterpart of '외국인' (foreigner) and is used in news and politics when a country refers to its own people. In everyday speech a Korean might also say '우리 국민'. Unlike '한국인', it does not name a country; it means whichever country the speaker is talking about.

examples.en: Income redistribution is carried out through taxes and welfare.

examples.ko: 일이 한쪽에만 몰려서 업무 재분배가 필요해요.
examples.en: Work is piled on one side, so the workload needs to be redistributed.
The team leader promised to redistribute the work.

examples.ko: 재분배 과정에서 불만이 나오지 않게 기준을 먼저 정했어요.
examples.en: We set the criteria first so that complaints wouldn't arise during redistribution.

examples.ko: 이익 재분배에 대한 의견이 서로 달라서 회의가 길어졌어요.
examples.en: Opinions on profit redistribution differed, so the meeting ran long.

examples.ko: 재분배 방식이 공정한지 직원들이 계속 물었어요.
examples.en: The employees kept asking whether the redistribution method was fair.

explain: 이미 나눈 것을 다시 나누거나 한쪽에 몰린 것을 고르게 나눌 때 써요. '소득 재분배', '업무 재분배'처럼 앞에 명사가 붙는 일이 많고, 뉴스에서 '소득 재분배'를 자주 들을 수 있어요.

phrases.en: The government announced an income redistribution policy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 가장 많이 듣는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation heard in the news.

phrases.en: This year there was a budget redistribution among departments.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 나눈 돈을 다시 나눌 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when money already allocated is divided again.

phrases.en: The employees asked for a redistribution of work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고르게 다시 나누자고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when asking for things to be shared out more evenly.

explain_en: Use it when dividing again what has already been divided, or spreading out something concentrated on one side. A noun often comes before it, as in '소득 재분배' (income redistribution) or '업무 재분배' (work redistribution), and you often hear '소득 재분배' in the news.

examples.en: This rule applies to all students.
The discount hasn't been applied yet.
The new law takes effect from next month.
It's the price with the coupon applied.
There are cases where exceptions apply.

examples.ko: 배운 내용이 실생활에 적용될 때 재미있어요.
examples.en: It's fun when what you learned is applied to real life.

explain: 규칙, 할인, 설정이 어떤 대상에 실제로 닿을 때 써요. '학생에게 적용되다'처럼 누구에게 해당하는지를 같이 말해요. '적용하다'는 사람이 그것을 쓰는 것이고, 적용되다는 그것이 저절로 걸리는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: This discount doesn't apply to new products.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해당되지 않는 경우를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something does not apply to a certain case.

phrases.en: Please read the newly applied rules.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used to modify a noun that follows.

phrases.example: 이 규칙의 적용 대상은 모든 직원이에요.
phrases.en: The people this rule applies to are all employees.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누구에게 해당하는지 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for saying who something applies to.

explain_en: Use it when a rule, discount, or setting actually reaches something. Say who it covers with 에게, like 학생에게 적용되다. 적용하다 is when a person uses it; 적용되다 feels like it kicks in on its own.

dis.h: rule or method takes effect on something

p.n: The other verb means adapting a principle to a field, so it does not fit a rule applying to people.

examples.en: This abbreviation is widely used on the internet.
In that country, dollars were accepted too.
I learned the greetings commonly used in Korea.

examples.ko: 이 방법은 다른 나라에서도 통용될 거예요.
examples.en: This method will be accepted in other countries too.

examples.ko: 그 말이 회사에서 통용돼서 저도 쓰기 시작했어요.
examples.en: That word was common at work, so I started using it too.
This card is accepted everywhere.

explain: '통용되다'는 말·돈·규칙이 어떤 장소나 집단에서 널리 받아들여질 때 써요. '사용되다'는 그냥 쓰인다는 뜻이고, '통용되다'는 거기서 통한다는 느낌이 더 강해요. 보통 '에서'와 같이 쓰여요.

phrases.example: 이 말은 젊은 사람들 사이에서 널리 통용돼요.
phrases.en: This word is widely used among young people.
phrases.nuance_ko: '널리'를 붙여 많은 곳에서 통한다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 'widely' says it is accepted in many places.

phrases.example: 이 카드는 일부 가게에서는 통용되지 않아요.
phrases.en: This card is not accepted at some stores.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 곳에서는 통하지 않는다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say something doesn't work in certain places.

phrases.en: This word is an expression commonly used in daily life.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에 붙여서 널리 쓰이는 말이라고 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed before a noun to describe commonly accepted usage.

explain_en: 통용되다 is for words, money, or rules that are widely accepted in a certain place or group. 사용되다 just means something is used, while 통용되다 adds the sense that it works there. It usually appears with 에서.

examples.ko: 이번 신제품이 휴대폰 시장의 판도를 바꿀 거예요.
examples.en: This new product will change the landscape of the phone market.

examples.ko: 선거 결과에 따라 정치 판도가 달라질 수 있어요.
examples.en: The political landscape could change depending on the election result.

examples.ko: 올해 리그 판도는 아직 예측하기 어려워요.
examples.en: It's still hard to predict how this year's league will play out.

examples.ko: 게임 업계의 판도에 큰 변화가 생겼어요.
examples.en: A big change has come over the landscape of the game industry.

examples.ko: 시장 판도도 곧 바뀔 것 같아요.
examples.en: The market landscape seems likely to change soon too.
The market has now entered a three-way contest.

explain: 주로 정치, 시장, 스포츠에서 세력이 어떻게 나뉘어 있는지, 그 전체 구도를 말할 때 써요. '판도가 바뀌다', '판도를 흔들다', '판도를 뒤집다'가 자주 쓰는 짝이에요. 비슷한 말로 '판세', '구도'가 있어요.

phrases.example: 새 선수가 오면서 리그 판도가 바뀌었어요.
phrases.en: The league landscape changed when the new player arrived.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세력 구도가 달라질 때 가장 많이 쓰는 짝이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for when the balance of power shifts.

phrases.example: 선거 판세가 아직 어떻게 될지 몰라요.
phrases.en: We still don't know how the election situation will turn out.
phrases.nuance_ko: '판도'와 비슷하지만 지금 이기고 지는 상황에 더 가까워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '판도' but closer to the current winning or losing situation.

phrases.en: The last game turned the whole picture upside down.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기존 구도를 완전히 바꿔 놓을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the existing order is completely overturned.
phrases.en_equiv: to overturn the balance of power

explain_en: It is mainly used in politics, markets and sports for the overall structure of how power is divided. Common pairings are '판도가 바뀌다', '판도를 흔들다' and '판도를 뒤집다'. Similar words are '판세' and '구도'.
